title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended processes for enterprise onboarding across Support, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues & Workarounds, and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and SRE partners. Follow these procedures to ensure predictable onboarding, fast time-to-value, and clear escalation paths for enterprise customers.

Key goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-production-call to <= 14 days for medium complexity integrations.
- Ensure deterministic escalation SLA adherence: initial response in 1 business hour for P1, resolution SLA targets documented below.
- Provide standard artifacts for handoff into Post-Onboarding Support and Quarterly Health reviews.

Table of contents:
1) Roles & Responsibilities
2) Onboarding Phases & Checklist
3) Integration Guide (high-level)
4) Escalation Playbook (SLA & Runbook links)
5) Known Issues & Workarounds
6) Health Checks and QBR Agenda
7) Artifacts, Templates & Links

1) Roles & Responsibilities
- Customer Success (owner): primary contact for onboarding plan, cadence, and QBRs.
- Solutions Engineering / Integration (owner): responsible for integration design, API verification, auth, and sample prompts/evals.
- Support Engineering (owner): triage and L2 troubleshooting during onboarding window (first 90 days).
- SRE / Platform (consulted): capacity, quota adjustments, and performance triage.
- Customer Technical Lead (customer): application owner for integration and acceptance testing.

RACI (summary):
- Planning & Kickoff: CSM (R), SE (A), Customer TL (C)
- API Integration & Test: SE (R), Customer TL (A), Support Eng (C)
- Production Cutover: CSM (R), SE (A), SRE (C)

2) Onboarding Phases & Checklist
Intro: Standard onboarding timeline is 2-6 weeks depending on workload complexity. Use this checklist and mark completion in the onboarding tracker.

Phase A — Kickoff (Day 0-3):
1. Conduct kickoff call (attendees: CSM, SE, Customer TL, Security if required).
2. Share onboarding plan + milestones in shared doc (deliverable: Onboarding Plan v1).
3. Confirm account access, API keys, and RBAC roles.

Phase B — Integration & Testing (Day 3-14):
1. Validate connectivity to Redwood API (region-specific endpoints).
2. Verify auth flows (API key, mTLS, or token exchange).
3. Run baseline smoke tests: generation, chat, embeddings (sample prompts attached).
4. Establish performance targets (latency p50/p95, throughput).
5. Provide sample eval set for quality baseline.

Phase C — Pilot / Canary (Day 7-28):
1. Deploy canary traffic (1-5% production).
2. Monitor for errors, latency, cost-per-token.
3. Iterate model choices / quantization profiles if cost or quality concerns arise.

Phase D — Production Cutover & Handoff (Day 14-42):
1. Execute cutover checklist (rollback plan, traffic ramp schedule).
2. Handoff to Support (owner list, on-call rotation).
3. Schedule first 30/60/90 day health checks and QBR cadence.

Minimum acceptance criteria (customer sign-off):
- Successful generation and embedding workflows for representative prompts.
- Error rate <= 1% for SLO-relevant endpoints under pilot load.
- Agreed latency/throughput baselines documented in the plan.

3) Integration Guide (high-level)
This section summarizes the typical integration steps and common pitfalls. Detailed API docs live in the public Redwood API docs (link below).

Mandatory steps:
- Auth: Confirm subscription and API key provisioning. For Private deployments, confirm KMS/HSM key access and network routes (VPC peering or on-prem proxies).
- Endpoints: Use region-specific endpoints; verify DNS resolution and TLS certificate chain.
- Sample requests: Run 3-generation, 3-chat, and 3-embedding calls to validate. Include content length and tokenization checks.
- Rate limits: Confirm expected request concurrency; request quota increases through the CSM via account team.

Network & Security checklist (example table):
- Firewall rules: allow outbound to api.redwood.ai:443 (or private endpoint).
- IP allowlist: if customer requires, collect proxy/egress IPs list.
- Mutual TLS: enable and verify certificate rotation schedule.

Dev / Test commands (examples):
- curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"Hello"}'
- Example SDK usage snippet and local test harness are provided by SE during integration.

4) Escalation Playbook (SLA & Runbook links)
Severity definitions & SLA targets:
- P1 (SEV0): Production outage or data loss impacting core product flows. Initial response: 1 business hour; incident declared; aim for mitigation within 4 hours (varies by contract).
- P2 (SEV1): Major degradation (latency >2x SLO or 50% error rate). Initial response: 2 business hours; mitigation target: 24 hours.
- P3 (SEV2): Functional bug with workaround. Initial response: 8 business hours; resolution in next release cycle.
- P4 (SEV3): General product question or enhancement request. Response per standard support SLA (2 business days).

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage by Support Engineer (within initial response window): collect logs, request IDs, sample payloads, timestamps, region, model and config.
2. If unresolved within escalation window (P1: 30 minutes after triage), escalate to SRE and SE on-call.
3. If service-level impact, declare incident and follow incident communications template (include incident bridge, public status page update, and customer communication).
4. Post-incident: create postmortem with timeline, root cause, and action items. Assign owners and target dates.

Required artifacts to attach to escalations:
- Full request/response with request_id (anonymize PII).
- Relevant logs (proxy, ingress, and runtime), p95 latency heatmaps, and recent deployment ids.
- Recent model/version config and quantization profile.

Runbook links (internal):
- Triage runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/triage-runtime-errors
- Network troubleshooting: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/network-troubleshooting
- Incident comms template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms

5) Known Issues & Workarounds
This section lists recurring issues observed during enterprise onboarding and pragmatic workarounds. Operational owners should keep this list updated.

Issue: Intermittent high latency for long-context generation
- Symptom: p95 latency spikes when context > 8k tokens.
- Root cause (common): KV cache thrash and non-optimal kernel selection for long sequences.
- Workarounds:
  - Use streaming responses to reduce perceived latency for the client.
  - Pin to a long-context optimized model variant (rwd-long-8k) during pilot.
  - Adjust batching window to reduce cache invalidation.

Issue: Elevated token billing from repeated eval traffic
- Symptom: Customer sees unexpected cost spike during large-scale evals.
- Workarounds:
  - Use smaller eval batches and enable caching for deterministic prompts.
  - Suggest offline evaluation using local quantized runtime (SE-assisted).
  - Apply temporary quota cap and schedule controlled runs with CSM approval.

Issue: Failed embeddings for very large documents (>1M chars)
- Symptom: API returns 413 or times out.
- Workarounds:
  - Chunk documents into <= 512k char segments and dedupe before embedding.
  - Use incremental embedding pipeline with checkpointing.

6) Health Checks and QBR Agenda
Health Check cadence (first 90 days): 30-day, 60-day, 90-day formal check-ins. After 90 days, transition to QBR cadence (quarterly unless contract stipulates otherwise).

30/60/90 Day Health Check template (CSM to prepare):
- Executive summary: adoption highlights, open risks, and next steps.
- Usage metrics: tokens consumed, API error rate, latency p50/p95, model variants used.
- Quality metrics: eval set pass rate, regression alerts if any.
- Costs: unit economics, cost-per-1000 tokens, and suggested optimizations.
- Action items & owners: prioritized list with due dates.

QBR agenda (60-90 minutes):
1. Introductions and objectives (5 minutes)
2. Executive summary: adoption, ROI highlights (10 minutes)
3. Usage trends and performance (15 minutes)
4. Quality & safety: eval results, regressions (15 minutes)
5. Operational review: incidents, escalations, and reliability (10 minutes)
6. Roadmap alignment & feature asks (10 minutes)
7. Next steps and success metrics (5 minutes)

Deliverables after QBR:
- QBR slide deck (shared within 3 business days).
- Updated onboarding health tracker and actions assigned in the success plan.
